::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Source notes (archive cell 8, unchanged)

Move from waves, pitch, simple oscillators to: voices and instruments, which form ensembles". But the nature of these sounds is different; A4 sung and A4 struck on the violin are the same A4—but we don't mistake the two.

Here, we introduce the concept of resonance; extend the complex exponential discussion to discuss damped (e.g., a kick drum waveform -> spiral) and driven (resonant) oscillators; the source-filter model (noise or harmonically rich sounds through filters -> vowel-like sounds); guitars, violins, same thing; tube model, vowels and formants.

- Resonance and Voices
    - Timbre and harmonics
    - Source, filter, and voices + instruments
    - Tube model, vowels, and formants
:::

## Plan

| Section | Content | hljod demo |
|---|---|---|
| Timbre and harmonics | Same pitch, different sources; a tone as many turning points at whole-number multiples of a base rate; the overtone series | harmonic toggler, harmonics table, overtone series (`edm-2`); square vs `gm_trumpet` on the same notes (`edm-7`) |
| Resonance | Damped oscillation as the inward spiral; driven oscillation; a high-Q filter as a lightly damped resonator, up to self-oscillation | 808 decaying sine and decay sweep (`edm-4c`); `.lpf().lpq()` Q table (`edm-2`) |
| Source, filter, voices + instruments | Harmonic or noisy source through filters; one bandpass ≈ one formant; a swept band sounds vowel-like | swept `.bpf()` on a sawtooth (`edm-2`); Moog oscillator → filter → amp chain |
| Tube model, vowels, formants | Throat → tube → wave equation → quarter-wave resonances → constrictions → nomogram → two-tube estimates → Kelly–Lochbaum | Pink Trombone (link); planned OJS tube and nomogram widgets |

**Suggested transition in →** from Waves' last step: one pitch from a voice is many turning points at
multiples of a base rate.

**Suggested transition out →** the tube's formants scale together with 1/length — that assumption is
what formant normalization in Isoclines relies on, and it is also a scaling symmetry that returns in
What's in a Wave.
